ambiguities.evidence: The Section 1.3 sentence contains no integrability or L² qualifier, while Section 1.1 defines variance through E(X − E X)².
ambiguities.impact: A formalization must decide whether the identity is restricted to finite real-valued variances or interpreted with extended values; adding finite-variance assumptions may reduce the literal applicability of 'any' but may be required by the chosen variance API.
ambiguities.issue: The sentence says 'any independent random variables' without explicitly stating finite second-moment assumptions.

contract_plain_english: For any finite independent family of real random variables for which the variances are meaningful, the variance of their sum is the sum of their variances; the variables need not share a distribution.

definitions_and_conventions: The ellipses denote the finite sum over indices i = 1, ..., N.
hypotheses: The expectations and variances occurring in the displayed identity are defined.
implicit_context: The variables share a probability space so their sum and joint independence are meaningful.
The phrase 'independent random variables X₁, ..., X_N' carries its standard joint-independence meaning.

details: The variance of the unscaled finite sum equals the finite sum of the individual variances.
There are no covariance or cross terms in the stated identity.
Independence is an explicit source hypothesis.
The source does not substitute identical distribution for independence.
The assertion applies to every finite independent family, not only to identically distributed variables.

undebatable_constraints: The conclusion is an equality, not an inequality or asymptotic statement.
The left side is the variance of the full unnormalized sum.
The right side is the sum of each individual variance.
Identical distribution and a common mean or variance are not hypotheses of this claim.
The family is finite and indexed from 1 through a positive integer N.
